speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I see you have increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, along with painful urination and a history of a swollen left ankle. To understand what is happening, how long have you been experiencing the current knee and urinary symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (Reiter's Syndrome) due to a preceding genitourinary infection (e.g., Chlamydia).

The combination of asymmetric oligoarthritis (knee and ankle), urethritis (painful urination), and recent sexual activity strongly suggests Reactive Arthritis. I would like to confirm the duration of the sexual activity and rule out other STIs. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Culture, and NAAT for Chlamydia/Gonorrhea.
